_how_to: Copy this file to playbooks/<your-id>.json, fill it in, then run: python3 ~/.gemini/config/skills/acq/acq.py playbook validate <your-id>. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.
name: One line: who has which problem

offer.title: What you will do for them, in plain words
offer.summary: One or two sentences about the deliverable.
offer.paid_next_step: What they can buy after the free sample.
offer.deliverable: What the sample is (video, mockup, PDF ...)

target.description: Who this is for and where you find them. Do not target platforms whose rules forbid scraping or off-platform contact.

_discovery: source: google_places (needs queries; uses the shared free Places budget) | urls | csv (you pass --urls/--csv to `acq find`).
_checks: Types: element (HTML tags), link (href regex), text (visible-text regex), count (images or tags, min/max), jsonld_type (schema.org types), https, manual (a person verifies in the browser and records a source URL). hit_if 'absent' means the condition is true when nothing is found. Add 'problem' to the checks that describe what you will fix.

checks.label: Thing you look for
checks.problem: Plain description of the problem a client would recognize

checks.label: Willingness-to-pay signal
checks.instructions: How to verify in a browser and which URL to record with --source-url.

hypotheses: Possible benefit you have NOT measured. It will always be labelled as unverified.
_sample_types: video | image | mockup_page | pdf_report | document | none

sample.label: Honest caption shown with the sample (what it is made from, that it is private).
sample.instructions: How the agent builds the sample, from which assets, with which local tool.

message.guidance: Tone and structure for the agent writing the message.
